source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: In the zylor of the xarv, amidst the thronged ziptu and the wheeled vorgons lining the larnax, the skymas bustled about the thraly desk, weaving past the huddled yexors; monitors blinked, fluids dripped, a cloth barrier was pulled aside. They worked diligently, the staff's actions synchronized, each motion precise, every word clipped. The room hummed with activity, each action measured, each second counted. Here stood a beleaguered physician, whose gaze darted restlessly, assessing the chaos. Each patient was marked, each moment accounted for, the rush unending. In this flurry, they moved, each one driven by the rhythm of the emergency.

In the rushhour ward, beside the triage desk sat the bustling nurse, coordinating the flow. Amidst the clamor, outside the main bay, the gurneys lined up, each bearing their own story. The swift nurse, amidst the urgent calls, directed the patients. With each page echoing through the halls, she swiftly managed the chaos. From the corridor came the sound of footsteps, echoing through the quieted air. Nurses moved swiftly, tending to the distressed, while forms filled in the background. A patient, visibly anxious, paced near the registration desk, his companion beside him murmuring complaints. The doctor, arriving promptly, assessed the situation, her eyes scanning over the charts. Across the room, monitors beeped steadily, a backdrop to the relentless pace. In the midst of the din, every minute counted, as the nurse deftly navigated each case. With every wristband placed, the process continued seamlessly.

In the thronged ward of Starglow Hospital, the bustling nurses moved amidst the rows of wheeled beds.

Amidst the clamor, six anxious patients awaited under the stern gaze of Dr. Varkin, while an urgent intercom buzzed for someone named Elvire to report immediately to bay three; simultaneously, the harried nurse, flustered by the ceaseless stream of emergencies, hurriedly updated patient charts and dispatched another nurse to fetch fresh saline solutions.

Nurses darted about swiftly, around monitors flickering, through corridors lined with restless gurneys and drawn curtains, amidst the din of intercom calls and murmurs of complaints from those waiting too long. Time seemed to stretch as each nurse, burdened with forms and wristbands, moved with calculated haste, their feet barely touching the floor. Outside, shadows loomed under the harsh lights, blending the lines between urgency and despair. One patient, pale and anxious, gripped the armrests of their chair with white-knuckled fingers, their companion beside them looking equally unsettled. The atmosphere pulsed with tension, a symphony of sighs and whispers carried on the air, mingling with the rhythmic beeping of machines. In the midst of the chaos, the doctor, flanked by nurses, assessed another case, the urgency palpable in every gesture, every hurried word. In the bustling ward, behind a desk, stood the nurse, overseeing myriad tasks. Nurses swiftly moved around the room, wheeling patients from chair to bed, checking monitors, drawing curtains, while a patient groaned softly, their visitor murmuring complaints under their breath about lengthy waits amid the clatter of carts and the hum of machinery. The doctor approached, paging urgently through forms, speaking briskly into the intercom. Patients awaited triage, their expressions tense, watches checked repeatedly. In every corner, the air thickened with anticipation, each person weighed down by silent pleas, their stories lost in the clamor of the urgent.

Amidst the flurry, amidst the chaos, amidst the cries for help, amidst the rush, amidst the struggle, amidst the tension.

Every chair filled, every bed occupied, every nurse engaged, each task performed with precision and care, each patient attended with urgency.

Companions paced, anxiety etched deep, watching clocks, their faces strained, questioning every delay with rising unease. Voices rose, echoing complaints, mingling with the din of machines beeping, their urgency marked by terse intercom calls.

One nurse, calm and steady, placed a wristband on a patient’s arm, noting details on clipboards with swift, sure strokes, her movements fluid, each step calculated. Patients’ fates were noted, their conditions assessed, each detail captured in clinical precision.

In the corner, a young woman wrung her hands, her husband pale beside her, his breaths quickening, a sign of distress. The nurse approached, clipboard at hand, her voice steady, her tone reassuring, guiding them through each step of the process.

The intercom buzzed again, its urgency clear, as another call rang out, summoning doctors to a case severe. Each page signaled a race against time, a battle waged silently within walls that bore witness to countless dramas of life and death.

In the midst of it all, time seemed to stretch and twist, each moment felt like hours. Yet, despite the rush, calm was maintained, each nurse and doctor knew their role, their tasks clear as day, their resolve unwavering.

At the heart of the ward stood the desk, flanked by nurses, where charts gathered.

Among the crowded gurneys lay patients; some groaned softly, others stared blankly, a few had been there longer, beneath the hum of machines, while a lone doctor moved briskly, his steps marked by urgent calls, each echoing off the walls, beyond which, somewhere, a clock chimed.

Companions paced.

One nurse bustled over, her pace steady, addressing the silent watch, their faces etched with worry.

They whispered, she answered with brisk nods, each glance directed to the door.

There, amidst the chaos, a murmur rose, sharp with impatience.

We wait, they murmured again, voices low yet insistent.

The day nurse, noting the tension, stepped towards them, her manner calm, her tone measured, addressing their concern.

She assured, promising soon, even as another nurse approached, bearing news of an immediate need elsewhere, her words a cascade of reassurance and redirection.

They listened, hope mingling with the familiar hum.
